name: Sacramento State Green
lede: Sacramento State Green is the near-black forest green of California State University, Sacramento's Hornets athletics, listed alongside white as a primary color rather than taken from any dye or pigment.

sections.title: A university's own green
sections.body:
The university's teams are the Hornets, and their primary colors are listed as green and white; a team-color reference site gives this dark green as Pantone PMS 343 at this hex [1]. Our library sources the name and value from a Wikipedia-style extended color list rather than from a dye or mineral word, so it is filed here as a place and institution name, not a pigment one [2]. No source consulted explains why this particular dark green, rather than a brighter or more common "hunter green," was chosen for the school [1].

By our look-alike data the nearest color is [[phthalo-green|Phthalo Green]], 2.8 units away and read as almost the same, with [[dark-hunter-green|Dark Hunter Green]] further off at 5.1, read as lighter [3]. It is much darker than a generic hunter green, about 13 units away [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a green within range of this hex in 15 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.06 percent, as photographed [4]. The earliest is an anonymous 1460 triptych of the Crucifixion, where it covers about 15 percent of the panel, and the strongest match is Bronzino's 1545 *Portrait of Giovanni de' Medici as a Child*, where it covers about 47 percent [4]. The United States and France carry a disproportionate share of the hits relative to their size in the archive, though on a small base of 15 paintings total [4]. Paintings from the 1800s hold the largest raw count, eight of the fifteen, but the sample stays too thin to call that a real decade effect [4]. As with any museum photograph, the match is to the image as scanned, not to a pigment sample from the canvas [4].

issues: Fixed two factual errors against the cited teamcolorcodes.com page: the Pantone number was wrong (article said PMS 627 C; the source lists this green as PMS 343) and the paired color was wrong (article said 'green and gold'; the source lists the primary colors as 'green and white'). Corrected both in the body, lede, aside.origin, and note 1.
Pantone PMS 343 and the hex come from a team-branding reference site, not an institutional style guide seen directly; hedged as web-sourced.
